request.title: Follow a request down the stack

steps.text: You ask an assistant a question in an app.
An agent decides it needs to look something up before answering.
Retrieval finds relevant documents and the prompt is assembled with the available tools.
The request reaches a serving endpoint and joins a batch with other users' requests.
The model's weights score every possible next token, one token at a time.
Not on the request path: training data shaped the model long before. Fresh documents came from retrieval instead.
The serving cluster schedules the work onto available accelerators.
GPUs stream the weights from memory and do the matrix maths.
All of it runs on electricity and cooling inside a data centre.
Power, cooling and fabricated chips make large-scale compute possible.
Accelerators turn electricity into massively parallel maths.
Clusters make that compute rentable and schedulable at scale.
Data is collected, cleaned and prepared for training.
Training on that data with that compute produces a foundation model.
Serving and optimisation make the model fast and affordable to use.
Retrieval and tools connect the model to your data and actions.
Agents chain those capabilities into multi-step work.
Applications deliver it to people, and their usage feeds back down.
